column2: My first ever electronics project was an altoids tin with two 9Vs, a 7805, and a USB port on a piece of protoboard I found in my grandfather's old electronics parts bins. I followed an Instructable to make it. After that, I was hooked. My next project was a dice roller I got from a copy of Make magazine. I ordered most of the parts off digikey. I loved the little projects in Make magazine, I thought it was so cool that you could just build your own electronics.

It's crazy; some years ago (many?) there were so many Alroids projects. I even wanted to buy a few tins of mints just to use the boxes (not that I dislike the cinnamon ones - or the quick rusting not withstanding).

I remember, there used to be powerbanks, buck-boost converters, joule theives, a ton of simple but cool projects.

I wonder where that vibe died. (Or if it transformed into something else?)

Very cool project. It's awesome to see young people in particular get involved in electronics.
